fields.statement: QA at e443109e, built binary in a scratch repo: rhiza request --milestone ms, by full ID and by short ID prefix each queued with the milestone ID shown in request ls --json (and --dry-run --json, and api call request); --milestone naming a plain intent, a capability, a retired milestone (by ID) or an unknown handle exited 2 with a usage error and queued nothing. The human request ls lines do not show the milestone.

QA at e443109e, built binary with fake rex/claude: two requests (one --milestone ms, one without); rhiza daemon --once started both plan runs; the fake claude logged RHIZA_MILESTONE=<ms ID> for the first run and unset for the second, and the session records carry milestone accordingly.

QA at e443109e, built binary: rhiza tui app requests driven in tmux. n shows the entry with milestone: auto; a request filed at auto queued with no milestone; ctrl+o then ms filed a request whose milestone is the ms ID in request ls --json; ctrl+o then area showed the usage error in the app and queued nothing.

QA at e443109e: rhiza guide plan from the built binary says the serves link must reach a milestone directly or through an intent under one, naming RHIZA_MILESTONE, the open milestone it fits, and never an umbrella or area intent under no milestone; go test ./internal/guide passes.

QA at e443109e, built binary, built-in plan workflow, fake claude as planner: serves a plain intent (area) or no serves link -> run ends failed at milestone-check naming the change set, never enters review; serves ms directly, or a landed intent under ms -> milestone-check passes, review entered. But serving a NEW intent under ms written into the plan change set itself (as the plan guide allows) -> milestone-check fails with serve no milestone: the check reads only the landed view, so the unlanded intent has no path to the milestone.
